canonical_statement: The primary objective was to determine cefazolin clearance during short daily hemodialysis; secondary objectives were to characterize cefazolin pharmacokinetics and assess whether current dosing recommendations produced adequate serum concentrations.

This was a prospective, open-label pharmacokinetic study conducted at the University Health Network Toronto Rehabilitation Institute, with recruitment and sampling from February 2013 through November 2014.
Eligible participants were adults receiving regular SDHD who were noninfected; exclusions included penicillin/cephalosporin allergy and cefazolin treatment within the prior 2 weeks.

population.label: Eligible adults receiving regular SDHD
exclusion_criteria: Cefazolin treatment within 2 weeks before study initiation

canonical_statement: Ten noninfected participants receiving short daily hemodialysis completed the study.

population.label: Study participants receiving short daily hemodialysis

canonical_statement: The 10 participants had median age 69 years (IQR 61-74), median body weight 75 kg (IQR 63-86), and median BMI 27 kg/m² (IQR 23-30); 6 were male and 4 female.

population.label: Study participants receiving short daily hemodialysis

canonical_statement: Study SDHD used 2-hour sessions 6 days per week with high-flux F80A dialyzers, blood flow 350 mL/min, and dialysate flow 800 mL/min.

exposures.details: 2-hour sessions, 6 days/week, high-flux F80A dialyzer; blood flow 350 mL/min and dialysate flow 800 mL/min

canonical_statement: Cefazolin was given as 1 g intravenously over 20 minutes immediately after dialysis on study days 1 and 2.

exposures.details: Administered immediately after SDHD on study days 1 and 2

canonical_statement: On study day 2, six blood samples were collected at 0, 1, 2, 2.33, at least 4, and 24 hours from dialysis initiation, and two dialysate samples were collected at 1 and 2 hours.
Cefazolin concentrations were measured by HPLC; the assay had 4% variance, and a one-compartment model with IV infusion and first-order elimination was used to derive pharmacokinetic parameters.
An in-practice model simulated cefazolin infused during the last 20 minutes of SDHD, using the same intradialysis and interdialysis elimination rate constants estimated from the study data.
The pharmacodynamic target used for efficacy assessment was a total cefazolin concentration of 40 mg/L, derived from an 8 mg/L free-drug breakpoint and an assumed 80% protein binding.

concept.text: Total plasma cefazolin concentration relative to 40 mg/L target

outcome.definition: Target total concentration >40 mg/L, corresponding to 8 mg/L free concentration under assumed 80% protein binding

canonical_statement: Adverse effects reported from cefazolin initiation through 2 weeks after the final dose were recorded with description, severity, and causal relationship.
Median intradialysis cefazolin clearance was 1.95 L/h (IQR 1.66-2.45).

canonical_statement: Observed plasma cefazolin concentration-time profiles were similar to the in-practice model that simulated administration during the last 20 minutes of dialysis.
The study was limited by its small sample size and loss of five of ten dialysate sample sets because of laboratory error.
The study did not assess steady-state concentrations and reported total rather than unbound free-drug concentrations.
Short drug-sampling intervals may have limited accurate estimation of elimination rates; the authors stated that population pharmacokinetic modeling would better address this limitation.

Participants were noninfected and showed substantial interpatient variation in residual renal function and BMI, limiting direct extrapolation to patients with serious infections and other patient profiles.
The authors concluded that cefazolin clearance during a 2-hour high-flux SDHD session was similar to that during a 4-hour conventional hemodialysis session.

The authors concluded that cefazolin 1 g IV during the last 20 minutes of SDHD or immediately after SDHD appeared adequate to maintain six times the Staphylococcus MIC for greater than 90% of the dosing interval.
